title: Savoy cyclone notice — Brenham Weekly Banner, June 17, 1880
text: The Denison News says people shook their heads when we published the account of a stone weighing a ton falling on the Rick farm, blown there by the Savoy cyclone but elder Kone goes us one better. In his services last Sunday his reverence spoke of sheep and cattle being carried through the air a distance of eighteen hundred miles by the cyclone. Elder, take our hat.
notes: This is a small clipping from the Brenham Weekly Banner, Vol. 15, No. 25, Thursday, June 17, 1880. It references and gently mocks exaggerated accounts of the Savoy cyclone, including a report by the Denison News of a one-ton stone blown onto the Rick farm, and a claim by 'Elder Kone' that sheep and cattle were carried 1,800 miles by the cyclone. The full newspaper page is not shown — only this small excerpt/clipping.
